title: Example 14-7: Verse Play with Extended Blank Space

illustrates.quote: Insert three blank cells between the speaker’s name and the beginning of the dialogue.

print.notes: Confirmed directly against the page image (compare-gold-14/pages/page-391.png): print shows a wide, print-typeset gap (not literal spaces) after 'SEBASTIAN:' and after the second 'ANTONIO:', with the dialogue beginning far to the right on the same line — the given braille inserts exactly three blank cells there (14.6.2a), shown here as three literal spaces in `text` for a forward-translation test (see resolution: Emboss cannot actually reproduce this, F-206).
print.printFeatures: Verse dialogue, speaker names in full caps followed by a colon; two of the four speaker turns have an extended blank space before the dialogue instead of an ordinary single space; continuation lines of the same speech are indented.

lines: ,if y b knew h[ y ! purpose *]i%
braille.notes: 1-5 margins for a speaker's first verse line (14.6.1a), 3-5 for a continuation line by the same speaker (14.6.1b); three blank cells (not one) separate 'SEBASTIAN:'/the second 'ANTONIO:' from their own dialogue, per 14.6.2a — confirmed in the page image by the print's own wide typeset gap at exactly those two points.

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on which two speaker turns carry the extended gap; A used a bare '\n' to separate a speech's own two verse lines inside one block (losing the per-line `level` this schema needs), B used '\n  ' (two literal spaces, an arbitrary indent amount); this reconciliation instead splits each speaker's own additional verse line into its own {kind:'speech', level:1} block, matching buildModel13/15's own established one-block-per-verse-line convention for every other poem/verse section, and lets the given braille's own 3-5 margin come from nestedMargins('poetry',...) rather than from a hard-coded string indent. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator ({type:'play', subtype:'verse'} blocks): every non-gap cell matches exactly, but the three blank cells collapse to ONE regardless of how many literal spaces `text` carries — confirmed directly (engine/louis.mjs's own translate() keeps a 3-space run intact; layout.mjs's wrapCells re-tokenises on every space and rejoins with a single one, `braille.split(' ').filter(w=>w.length>0)`, discarding the extra two unconditionally). This is a genuine, newly-documented Emboss gap (F-206, standards-findings.md) with no per-file workaround — EXPECTED MISMATCH, not a gold-file error (see differences.md).
